clue.text: Bloomers of the hour?

parts.note: bloomers here are flowering plants, not underwear, planted in a bed so that they show the time of day

explanation.surface: A joke about underwear that is fashionable right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests knickers, and 'of the hour' suggests the latest fashion; in fact it means flowers arranged to tell the hour, as in a park's floral timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden display of plants laid out as a dial, sometimes with working hands, shows the time.

clue.text: Cut over point brings one inelegant run

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes first, above it

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cut across a point leaves someone running clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, bounding stride covering ground with a loose, ungainly gait.

clue.text: Dahlia's nephew of whom Wodehouse wrote so amusingly

definitions.text: Dahlia's nephew of whom Wodehouse wrote so amusingly

parts.words: Dahlia's nephew of whom Wodehouse wrote so amusingly
parts.note: Aunt Dahlia in P. G. Wodehouse's comic novels has a hapless young nephew, Bertie, master of Jeeves

explanation.surface: A literary tribute to a comic character from P. G. Wodehouse's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dahlia' looks like a flower but is Bertie's aunt in Wodehouse's Jeeves stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie, the idle gentleman narrator of the Jeeves stories, is Aunt Dahlia's nephew.

clue.text: Telephoned for a horizontal bar?

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece of a ladder or chair

explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of the verb for calling by phone is also a ladder's crosspiece.

clue.text: Trouble about lower part of personal column?

definitions.text: Trouble about lower part of personal column?

parts.words: Trouble about lower part of personal column?
parts.note: the personal column is not newspaper small ads but one's own spinal column, and the trouble is pain at its lower end

explanation.surface: A complaint about the bottom of the newspaper's private ads section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal column' suggests a newspaper's classified ads; here it is your own backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the lower back, the lumbar region of the spine, is a common ailment.

clue.text: Money remitted by Speaker

indicators.note: the word is as said by a speaker, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: money remitted is sent to someone

explanation.surface: Funds transferred by the presiding officer of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' looks like the Commons officer but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth a hundredth of a dollar or euro is a small unit of currency.

clue.text: This jumper rides up

parts.note: the jumper is not a sweater that rides up the body but a person leaping from aircraft, who in fact rides down under a canopy

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sweater that keeps riding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater; it is someone who jumps from aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaps from a plane and descends under a canopy is a skydiving jumper.

clue.text: A very soft skin-cream for the office

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
an ointment is a cream rubbed on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone buys an extremely gentle moisturiser to use at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace but means a post or position held.
explanation.definitionFit: An office in the sense of a post someone is given is a job or position they are named to.

clue.text: Theologians' revised collections

indicators.note: the word Theologians' is revised, its letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Scholars of religion have updated their compilations.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthologies are published selections of poems or stories gathered together.

clue.text: One may sell pieces of Cavendish, according to report

definitions.text: One may sell pieces of Cavendish, according to report

parts.words: One may sell pieces of Cavendish, according to report
parts.note: Cavendish is a kind of pressed sweetened pipe smoke sold in plugs, so the seller is a shopkeeper, not a dealer in pieces of a stately home

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone is selling off parts of the Cavendish family estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavendish looks like the aristocratic family name but is a type of pipe leaf pressed into cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling cigarettes, cigars and pipe leaf trades in Cavendish.

clue.text: Given old money, young person prepared to look for ability in others

parts.note: a talent was a unit of money in the ancient world
a Scout, whose motto is 'Be Prepared', is a young member of the Scout movement

explanation.surface: Given a windfall, a youngster is ready to seek out gifted people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' is part of the Scout definition, from the motto Be Prepared; the answer is used here as a verb, to seek out gifted people.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a recruiter who seeks out gifted performers or players.

clue.text: Composer near to ruin

indicators.note: near is brought to ruin, wrecked so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician is on the verge of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was the eighteenth-century English composer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne is an English composer, best known for Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Address, we hear, through which Julius Caesar received his rents

definitions.text: Address, we hear, through which Julius Caesar received his rents

parts.words: Address, we hear, through which Julius Caesar received his rents
parts.note: said aloud, address is a dress, and the rents are the tears made in that garment by the daggers of the conspirators, not money from tenants

explanation.surface: A speech by which a Roman ruler collected the money his tenants owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' looks like income but means rips; 'Address, we hear' gives 'a dress', the Roman robe that Caesar's assassins stabbed through.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman robe worn by citizens is the garment Caesar wore when he was stabbed.

clue.text: Humiliated, dame has wandered off

indicators.note: the words dame has wander off from their order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly lady has strayed off and feels embarrassed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humiliated feels shame and embarrassment.

clue.text: Take Mike out, perhaps, to decontaminate

definitions.meaning: remove a hidden microphone, like Mike, from a room
rid something of insects or germs

explanation.definitionFit: Removing listening devices or insect pests both mean clearing a place of them.

clue.text: Di's concert, in a word, is rock

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Di's concert, in a word, is rock' for AGITATE: no parse of 'Di's concert, in a word' gives AGIT-, and no scan or search shows the printed text; likely an OCR misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Di's concert, in a word, is rock

clue.text: Sort of wit in "Room at the Top"?

definitions.meaning: The refined, elegant humour of ancient Athens
a loft, a room directly under the roof; Room at the Top is also a novel by John Braine

explanation.definitionFit: Athenian elegance of style gives a type of wit, and a loft is the room at a house's top.

clue.text: Clergyman has lost end of right-hand page

indicators.note: the clergyman's title loses its final letter, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar has mislaid the final page of his book.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the front of a leaf, on the right of an open book, is its odd-numbered page.

clue.text: Retain purchase

definitions.meaning: a firm grip or foothold, as in 'get a purchase on the rock'

explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to keep a grip on it, and a purchase is a grip or foothold.

clue.text: Improvised jazz? Run quickly!

definitions.meaning: wordless jazz singing made up on the spot
a command to go away fast, like 'shoo!'

explanation.definitionFit: Jazz vocalists improvise nonsense syllables, and the same word is an order to clear off at once.

clue.text: Notes for Orsino's love-feast?

definitions.meaning: Orsino in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night opens with 'If ... be the food of love, play on'

explanation.definitionFit: Notes make up a tune, and Shakespeare's Duke Orsino calls melody the food of love.

clue.text: Milliner Dot, semi-drunk

indicators.note: Dot and semi are drunk, staggering out of order

explanation.surface: A hat-maker called Dot is half-intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a maker of fashionable hats or dresses.

clue.text: Dear in France, holding a jolly attractive sort

indicators.note: the French word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: cher is French for dear
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A lovely person in France is grasping a cheerful, appealing type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is a delightful, captivating person.

clue.text: Language used to label a record

parts.note: a tag is a label fixed to something
a log is a written record, as of a ship's voyage

explanation.surface: Someone describes the vocabulary used to catalogue an archive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main language of the Philippines, on which Filipino is based.

clue.text: Church right to repair icon in very poor condition

indicators.note: the word icon needs repair, so its letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A church's rule is to restore a religious painting that has badly decayed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'chronic' means dreadful or very bad, not only long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage applies the word to anything dreadful or of very low quality.

clue.text: Shower in Slough, say?

definitions.meaning: to let fall or pour down, as trees let fall leaves
to slough is to cast off skin, as a snake does

explanation.definitionFit: Trees cast their leaves like a shower falling, and a snake casting its skin likewise drops it.

clue.text: Last of mulled draught found in Yorkshire

indicators.note: only the final letter of mulled is used

parts.note: draught beer, ale, is drawn from the cask

explanation.surface: The remains of a spiced warm beer are discovered in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the Yorkshire Dales are valleys famous enough that the county is synonymous with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire's broad valleys are its famous landscape, the Dales national park.

clue.text: A site, would you say, for fruit?

indicators.note: asks what the words sound like when said aloud

parts.note: a site is heard as 'a sight', something unattractive to look at

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a location suits growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A site' sounds like 'a sight', an unsightly thing; that gives a word for unsightly, which sounds the same as the Jamaican citrus fruit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine, has a lumpy, unlovely skin.

clue.text: Birthright-seller's name found in thesaurus

indicators.note: the name is found in the word that follows, running inside its letters

explanation.surface: A reference book of synonyms lists the name of a Bible figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Jacob's elder twin sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Isaac's elder son trades his inheritance rights to his brother Jacob for a meal.

clue.text: A quarter of peas Toby?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A portion of peas belongs to someone called Toby.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four compass points is a quarter of the compass.

clue.text: AA team guess incorrectly what is inside banger

indicators.note: the letters of AA team guess are put together incorrectly, so they form a new order

explanation.surface: A motoring breakdown crew wrongly guesses what is inside an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for both a sausage and a decrepit old car; the AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service, so the surface is all motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a sausage, and its filling is minced pork.

clue.text: Put off, I make a speech and go to pieces

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
to orate is to speak formally in public

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from speaking falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline, crumble or fall apart.
